quizName: DMV Practice Test #9 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When riding in a group, why should inexperienced riders be near the front?

options.text: Experienced riders can watch them more easily.
They will get lost if they are leading.
They may slow the group down as leaders.
They will ride too fast in any other position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Experienced riders can watch them more easily.
questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride near the front, just behind the leader. This lets experienced riders watch them easily.

questions.question: Riding in cold weather for long periods can cause all of the following, except:
questions.correctAnswerText: Hot flashes.
questions.explanation: Long rides in cold weather can cause severe chills, fatigue, and hypothermia. Wear proper clothing to protect yourself from the cold.

questions.question: If another driver is following you too closely, what should you do?

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them in front of you. If it is safe, change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up will only make them tailgate you at a higher speed.

questions.question: A person is legally intoxicated when their blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is _____ or higher.
questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent
questions.explanation: For adults over 21, a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher is legally intoxicated. Driving while intoxicated is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, what should you avoid?
questions.correctAnswerText: Braking quickly.
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, reduce your speed, avoid sudden movements, and use both brakes gently if you need to stop.

questions.question: What is the benefit of checking your motorcycle thoroughly?

options.text: It is only useful if done by a mechanic.
It should not be done before a ride.
It should only be done after a ride.
It helps find mechanical problems or equipment failures.

questions.correctAnswerText: It helps find mechanical problems or equipment failures.
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride. This helps you find mechanical problems or equipment failures that could be dangerous.

questions.question: What should passengers do on a motorcycle?

options.text: Sit as far back on the bike as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean when the operator leans.
questions.explanation: Passengers should sit directly behind the operator and lean with them. They should sit as far forward as they can without crowding the operator, and hold onto the operator's waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: How can you help a driver entering the highway from an entrance ramp?

options.text: Stay in your lane. It is not your responsibility to be seen.
Change to a different lane away from the entrance ramp, if possible.
Weave within your lane to be more visible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change to a different lane away from the entrance ramp, if possible.
questions.explanation: Give merging vehicles plenty of space. If possible, change lanes away from the entrance ramp. If you cannot change lanes, slow down to create space for the merging driver.

questions.question: How should you stop quickly?

options.text: Use the front brake first, then the rear brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, apply both brakes at the same time.

questions.question: What should you do if your motorcycle starts to wobble?

options.text: Grip the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Grip the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up during a wobble. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly, slow down by gradually closing the throttle, lean forward and down, and pull off the road. Do not use the brakes, as this can make the wobble worse.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When you can see through the vehicle in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the roadway is wet.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when your motorcycle needs more time to stop. Also increase it in heavy traffic or when you cannot see through the vehicle ahead.

questions.question: Most crashes happen during the day. What should you wear to reduce crash risk?
questions.correctAnswerText: Bright-colored clothing.
questions.explanation: Wear bright-colored clothing when riding to make yourself more visible to other drivers, even during the day.

questions.question: If hazards are on your left, where should you ride in the lane?

options.text: In the left portion of the lane.
In the right portion of the lane.
In any portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the right portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: When hazards are on your left, ride in the right portion of the lane. Adjust your position as road and traffic conditions change.

questions.question: When do most motorcycle crashes happen?
questions.correctAnswerText: On short trips.
questions.explanation: Most crashes happen on trips shorter than five miles, just a few minutes after the rider starts riding.

questions.question: How should you adjust your riding when carrying a passenger?

options.text: Keep a shorter following distance than when riding alone.
Brake later than you would when riding alone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride slower than usual.
questions.explanation: Extra passenger weight means your motorcycle needs more time to speed up, slow down, and turn. Reduce your speed, start slowing earlier, increase your following distance, and look for larger gaps when merging or crossing traffic.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When you can see through the vehicle ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the pavement is wet.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when your motorcycle takes longer to stop. Do this when the pavement is slippery, when you cannot see the vehicle ahead, or when traffic is heavy.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: When should you use the front brake?

options.text: Any time you slow or stop.
Only when slowing on slippery roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any time you slow or stop.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow or stop.

questions.question: Why should motorcycle riders not rely only on mirrors?

options.text: Motorcycle mirrors are too small to see much.
Motorcycles have blind spots, just like cars.
Mirrors distract you from the road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles have blind spots, just like cars.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots. You cannot rely only on mirrors to see what is behind you. Check your blind spots frequently by turning your head.

questions.question: What should you do when riding at night?

options.text: Be flexible about your lane position and adjust to conditions.
Travel faster than usual to reach your destination quickly.
Always use low beam headlights to see better.
Decrease your following distance to stay close to the vehicle ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be flexible about your lane position and adjust to conditions.
questions.explanation: Be flexible with your lane position, especially at night. Use safe riding strategies in less than ideal conditions.

questions.question: A motorcyclist should:

options.text: Use the brake throughout the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift gears before turning.
questions.explanation: Change gears before you enter a turn, not while turning.

questions.question: Making eye contact with other drivers:

options.text: Guarantees they will yield to you.
Does not mean they see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not mean they see you.
questions.explanation: A driver may look directly at you and still not notice you. Do not rely on eye contact to know that a driver sees you.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, tell them to:

options.text: Sit as far back as possible.
Put their feet on the muffler.
Get on after you start the engine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get on after you start the engine.
questions.explanation: Ask your passenger to get on only after you start the engine. They should sit close to you without crowding you and hold onto your waist, hips, or belt. They must keep both feet on the footrests at all times, even when stopped.

questions.question: To react faster to dangers, you should:

options.text: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
Pull in the clutch when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: In risky areas like intersections, parking lots, schools, and construction zones, keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes. This reduces the time you need to react to hazards.

questions.question: Reflective clothing should be worn:

options.text: During the day and at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: During the day and at night.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during daylight. Wear bright colors and reflective materials at all times to be more visible.
